subject: Q4 OKR: final verdicts, retro appendix, and publish plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: product@acme.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Q4 OKR: final verdicts, retro appendix, and publish plan

Team —

We're at the finish line for Q4 scoring. Attached is my suggested scoring matrix (OKR_scoring_matrix_Q4_v3.xlsx) with row-level evidence pointers and the exec narrative draft (exec_narrative_draft_v2.docx). Please do three things before EOD Wednesday (07/14):

1) Confirm or correct the score in column G for objectives you own, add one-line justification in column H.
2) Drop any final retrospective highlights / learnings into retrospective_notes_team-a_v1.pdf (or send via reply if short).
3) Flag any score you think needs an escalation or a different language treatment for the executive narrative.

Proposed calibration slot: Thu 07/15, 10:00–10:30 PT — I will send a short invite if we need it. If there's a single disputed score, we'll try to resolve asynchronously; if more than two disputes we hold the call.

Audience: execs + board packet goes out Friday morning; internal publish Thursday afternoon. External ask: Acme (copied) — we will share the customer-facing summary after the exec review; their renewal appendix will reflect final scores.

Attachments: OKR_scoring_matrix_Q4_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), exec_narrative_draft_v2.docx (docx)

Thanks —
Markus
Director, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: product@acme.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 OKR: final verdicts, retro appendix, and publish plan

Markus — thanks for the package. Quick notes:

- I updated Objective A.2 from 70% -> 85% (column G) based on the final telemetry that came in last week; added a one-line rationale in column H with the link to the query.
- For Objective B, I recommend softening the narrative language to "progress behind plan due to infra flakiness" rather than stronger wording; added a comment in the exec doc (see link).
- Attached my retro highlights as a short PDF; main items: cross-team onboarding gaps, 2 infra incidents that materially shifted delivery, and the feature flag rollforward that mitigated customer impact.

On disputes: I expect one hotspot (C.1) where product metrics exceeded our internal target but customer adoption stats were mixed — I left the score but added a note to escalate if Vivek wants a conservative adjustment.

Attachment: retrospective_notes_team-a_v1.pdf (pdf)

On Thu call: I can make 10:00 PT.

— Laura
VP, Growth & Product Ops

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, product@acme.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 OKR: final verdicts, retro appendix, and publish plan

Thanks — I reviewed Markus' matrix and Laura's notes. Two quick points:

1) Objective C.1 (adoption) — I agree with Laura that the raw metric looks good, but the downstream retention funnel is weak. I'd rather see the score lowered from 85 -> 70 and then call out the retention gap explicitly in the narrative. We should avoid language that signals product-market fit.

2) Narrative tone — please remove language that frames B as an "operational failure"; that will cascade into external comms. Suggest "delivery constrained by infra instability; mitigations implemented and monitoring added."

I've added inline comments to the Google doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-exec-narrative
HubSpot record for the customer context: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/companies/ACME-12345

If Laura and Markus are comfortable with the updated phrasing, I'm happy to endorse the scores. If not, we should take the calibration call Thu.

On disputes: marking C.1 as "discuss on call" in the matrix.

— Vivek
VP, Engineering

Short note — I'm aligned with Vivek on C.1. I've updated the matrix with one supporting customer quote and set the score to 70 (see column G).

If we want to close this without a call, I'm available Thu 10:00 PT for a 15-min calibration. Otherwise I will push the final matrix comments by 09:00 Thu.

— Marissa
Head of Customer Success

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: product@acme.com, Sandra Lewis <sandra.lewis@acme.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@consults.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 OKR: final verdicts, retro appendix, and publish plan

Perfect — thank you all for the quick turn. Summary / final decisions: 

- Objective C.1 final score: 70 (matrix updated). Rationale: strong launch metric but retention shortfall; narrative calls out follow-up plan and owner.
- Objective A.2 final score: 85 (Laura's telemetry note accepted).
- Objective B language: changed to "delivery constrained by infra instability; mitigations implemented" per Vivek.

Action items (owner -> due):
- Laura: update exec one-pager with the moderated wording and finish the one-line evidence bullets (due Thu 22:00 PT).
- Vivek: confirm retention remediation plan summary (due Fri 07/16 17:00 PT).
- Marissa: I'll include the customer quote in the customer appendix we share with Acme next week.
- Stephanie: publish internal OKR page (redwood-internal/docs/okrs) with matrix and retro appendix by Fri 09:00 PT.

Attaching final files: OKR_scoring_matrix_Q4_v3.xlsx (finalized), exec_narrative_draft_v2.docx (with accepted edits), retrospective_notes_team-a_v1.pdf.

External note: Acme — thanks for your patience. We'll share the customer-facing summary on Monday after exec review; nothing in the public-facing materials will expose internal mitigations beyond the agreed wording.

If anyone has last-minute evidence that changes these outcomes, flag the thread immediately. Otherwise I'll proceed to publish and circulate to execs and the board.

Thanks —
Markus
Director, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference
